title: The Educated Barbarian: Hagakure analysis (part. 9)
summary: NH continues his Hagakure commentary: fortune is random so take ownership of your response, keep your word like steel, pair visualization with action and break big dreams into small steps. He criticizes calculating cowards and 'erudite' fitness experts who never apply their knowledge, and urges meeting adversity with courage and jubilation, comparing it to training stress.
claims: Most things that happen to you are random rather than caused by good or evil forces; blaming a figure for them removes your ability to own and respond to them
Good and evil do not exist in nature, but moral notions are still useful because they hold society together like laws
Always uphold your word and promises; people will trust you and the steadfastness builds your own confidence and identity
Many people waste time changing paths and seeking least resistance; decide, do it fully and do not give up
Visualization works only when paired with action, like prayer must be accompanied by effort
People with the biggest dreams often do the least; project two years ahead rather than twenty and climb in smaller steps
The most intimidating men I have met were men in their 50s-60s who kept training or doing martial arts and accumulated confidence
If you are in your 20s and have already resigned yourself to mediocrity you have given up on life
Men are born to protect those who are biologically weaker, even if those people resent them
Avoid death but do not fear it; fear of death ruins quality of life, visible in old people who never accepted it
Fitness PhDs who look like twigs are theory without application, like an aviation degree holder who cannot fly
Purely intellectual fitness experts often resent physicality and shame others; novices overestimate them because they cite science
The real test is whether you can look at yourself in the mirror after what you have done, not public reputation
Meet adversity with courage and jubilation rather than self-pity, which only matches your mindset to the problem
Like bodybuilding, more stress handled means more growth: the more training stress you can handle, the bigger and stronger you get
